content.user_title: Plan Recruitment Marketing With Consent Controls
content.value_statement: Recruitment campaigns can confuse applicant processing with marketing permission and promote closed vacancies. This skill drafts campaign plans with explicit consent, audience rules and vacancy checks.
actual_capabilities: Draft separate campaign briefs for candidate job alerts, employer acquisition and employee communications.
Propose minimal optional capture forms that keep applicant records and protected traits outside marketing targeting.
Define audience segments using declared role preferences, location choices, marketing permission and lifecycle state.
Design journey entry, exits, re-entry and deduplication rules, including checks for closed vacancies and queued messages.
Specify campaign metrics, attribution windows, launch blockers and test cases for missing, duplicate, suppressed or stale records.
Outline platform mappings for verification against current provider documentation without inventing API payloads or account capabilities.
limitations: Provides planning guidance, not a bundled campaign sender, recruitment database or deployment integration.
Does not score candidates, determine employment eligibility or make hiring decisions.
Does not establish legal compliance; jurisdiction-specific requirements need qualified review.
Cannot assume live vacancy status, valid consent or platform capabilities without current verification.

use_cases.title: Plan Permission-Based Job Alerts
use_cases.description: Prepare an alert signup form and journey using voluntary job preferences, explicit permission and current vacancy checks.

use_cases.title: Build Employer Consultation Campaigns
use_cases.description: Outline employer lead capture and follow-up using business contact details without importing candidate records into marketing.

use_cases.title: Review Recruitment Campaign Readiness
use_cases.description: Define suppression rules, queued-message checks, test cases and launch blockers before approving a campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Job-Alert Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a weekly engineering job-alert brief for our careers site. Use voluntary role and location preferences. Separate applications from marketing subscriptions. List missing inputs and launch blockers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish a campaign purpose and permission boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design Talent-Community Capture
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose an optional talent-community form for a UK employer. Include minimal fields, permission wording, preference controls and a welcome message. Exclude CVs and protected traits. Flag wording for qualified legal review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a minimal capture form and draft copy.

prompt_templates.title: Specify Segments and Journey Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Using a synthetic schema, plan engineering alerts for subscribers who voluntarily selected remote work. Define eligibility, null handling, deduplication, exits and re-entry. Include missing-permission and closed-vacancy tests. Keep platform mappings provisional.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: translate campaign requirements into explicit audience and journey logic.

prompt_templates.title: Review Queued Campaign Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our proposed recruitment journey using anonymized event definitions and synthetic records. Cover consent refresh, stale vacancies, queued messages, multiple applications and service communications. Produce test cases, metrics and launch blockers. Do not activate or modify anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: review release readiness across consent, vacancy state and message queues.

output_examples.input: Plan a weekly remote engineering job alert with a separate talent-community signup.
output: Campaign: weekly engineering alerts for subscribers who voluntarily selected remote roles and explicitly permitted job-alert marketing.
Capture: email address, role-family preference, location preference and a clear permission choice; collect no CV or protected traits.
Send checks: confirm permission, suppression status and the authoritative vacancy listing immediately before delivery.
Exit: stop closed or filled vacancy promotions and cancel or suppress stale messages already queued.
Launch blocker: hold release if permission checks or vacancy refresh cannot be trusted.

output_examples.input: Outline a recruiting agency campaign to attract employers seeking hiring support.
output: Purpose: invite employers to a hiring-needs consultation, separate from candidate job alerts.
Capture: business contact details and hiring needs; keep candidate records in the authorized recruitment system.
Follow-up: identify the responsible owner, verify channel eligibility and keep consultation replies separate from unrelated promotions.
Claims review: omit placement, salary and visa sponsorship guarantees unless supported by current verified evidence.
Measurement: define valid consultation requests and an attribution window before launch.

best_practices: Provide campaign purpose, region, recruiting platform and follow-up owner; use anonymized schemas and synthetic records.
Verify channel-specific permission and live vacancy status before every send, including messages already queued.
Test suppressed, missing-data, duplicate, stale and conversion cases; obtain explicit authorization before any live changes.
anti_patterns: Treating an application, saved tag or test record as permission to send marketing.
Using protected traits, inferred proxies or click propensity to rank candidates or determine employment eligibility.
Launching campaigns with unverified provider behavior, unreliable exclusions or stale vacancy data.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It drafts campaign briefs, capture copy, segment rules, journey logic, metrics, test cases and launch blockers.

faq.question: Can it send campaigns or change subscriptions automatically?
faq.answer: It defaults to plans and local drafts. Live publishing, contact uploads, subscription changes and sends require explicit authorization for the target and scope.

faq.question: Does it evaluate or rank job applicants?
faq.answer: No. It covers recruitment communications, not candidate scoring, employment eligibility, automated screening or hiring decisions.

faq.question: Do I need Poptin?
faq.answer: No. Poptin is an optional capture-form reference. Keep the existing platform unless a verified gap justifies a change.

faq.question: Can I provide real applicant records?
faq.answer: Use anonymized schemas and synthetic examples for planning. Keep CVs, assessments, identity documents and other applicant records in the authorized recruitment system.

faq.question: Does the skill guarantee compliant recruitment advertising?
faq.answer: No. A qualified owner must review jurisdiction-specific requirements, and current provider documentation must confirm implementation details.
